title: Design a Global Social Media Newsfeed & Timeline Engine (300M DAU)

spark.summary: Design a 300M DAU social media newsfeed and timeline engine supporting 200K RPS feed reads (<150ms p99), 50M-follower celebrity posts, two-stage ML ranking, and duplicate-free cursor pagination.
spark.keyTakeaway: To keep the architecture evolvable without sacrificing reliability, separate ingestion (Kafka partitioned by AuthorID + Media CDN) from Hybrid Fan-Out (active-only Redis ZSETs + Celebrity Pull Cache), Two-Stage ML Ranking, and Snapshot Cursor Pagination.
spark.byteSummary:
Designing a 300M DAU social media newsfeed (e.g., X/Instagram scale) requires serving ~200K RPS feed reads under 150ms p99 while ingesting ~10K RPS posts—including viral celebrity posts with 50M+ followers. Storing and ranking billions of timeline entries in real time demands strict separation between ingestion, fan-out, hydration, and ML scoring.

The architecture spans four tiers: (1) Post Ingestion writing media to S3/CDN, metadata to sharded Cassandra/Postgres, and events to Kafka partitioned by `author_id`; (2) a Hybrid Fan-Out Service querying the Social Graph Service to push normal posts (<100K followers) to active followers' Redis Sorted-Set inboxes while routing celebrities to a Pull Cache; (3) a Two-Stage Feed Hydrator & Feature Store feeding a LightGBM/Two-Tower ML Ranker; and (4) a Seen-Post Bloom Filter + Snapshot Cursor Paginator.

Key trade-offs include pushing only to 14-day active followers to cut Redis RAM by 70%, and caching ranked page-1 snapshots for 10 minutes so pages 2..N scroll smoothly without re-running ML.

learningJourney.title: 300M DAU Capacity Sizing & Redis Inbox Memory
learningJourney.purpose: Calculate read/write QPS, Kafka fan-out throughput, and Redis RAM for active inboxes.

explanation.foundation: 300M DAU * 10 feed loads/day = 3B reads/day (~35K avg, ~200K peak RPS).
explanation.core: At 10K peak post writes/sec with avg 200 active followers, push fan-out generates ~2M Redis `ZADD` ops/sec.
explanation.deepDive: Keeping 800 `(post_id, ts)` entries (16B each = ~13KB) for 150M recently active users requires ~2TB of Redis Cluster RAM—completely feasible across ~40 memory-optimized nodes.

cards.label: Active-Only Savings

cards.label: Pipelined ZADD
cards.detail: Batch 100 ZADDs per Redis pipeline to cut network syscall overhead by 100x.

sectionDiagram.summary: Sizing active-user Redis inboxes at ~2TB makes precomputed timelines economical at 300M DAU.
sectionDiagram.caption: Pipelined Redis writes absorb 2M ZADDs/sec cleanly.

learningJourney.title: Post Ingestion, Media CDN & Author-Partitioned Kafka
learningJourney.purpose: Decouple heavy image/video uploads from lightweight timeline fan-out events.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Post Ingestion, Media CDN & Author-Partitioned Kafka** as the intuition layer for Design a Global Social Media Newsfeed & Timeline Engine (300M DAU): Decouple heavy image/video uploads from lightweight timeline fan-out events.
explanation.core: Clients upload images/videos directly to S3 via presigned URLs served behind CloudFront/Cloudflare CDN. The API Gateway validates the post, persists metadata to sharded Cassandra/MySQL (`posts` partitioned by `post_id`, `author_timeline` partitioned by `author_id`), and publishes a tiny `PostCreated` event to Kafka partitioned by `author_id`.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, post ingestion, media cdn & author-partitioned kafka becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Engineer 7-day rotating Seen-Post Bloom filters, 10m snapshot cursors, diversity decay, and non-jumping live pills.

sectionDiagram.title: Media CDN + Author-Partitioned Kafka

cards.label: Presigned Uploads
cards.detail: Keep multi-megabyte media bytes completely off the API/Kafka path.

cards.label: Per-Author Ordering
cards.detail: Partitioning Kafka by author_id preserves chronological order per creator.

sectionDiagram.summary: Direct-to-CDN media uploads keep the ingestion and Kafka fan-out path ultra-lightweight.
sectionDiagram.caption: Partitioning Kafka by author_id guarantees ordered timeline updates.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Design a Global Social Media Newsfeed & Timeline Engine (300M DAU) without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: To keep the architecture evolvable without sacrificing reliability, separate ingestion (Kafka partitioned by AuthorID + Media CDN) from Hybrid Fan-Out (active-only Redis ZSETs + Celebrity Pull Cache), Two-Stage ML Ranking, and Snapshot Cursor Pagination.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

decisionExercise.prompt: When Design a Global Social Media Newsfeed & Timeline Engine (300M DAU) experiences a sudden 5x traffic spike alongside a slow downstream dependency, which engineering choice best protects system stability?

options.label: Increase retry counts and remove client timeouts so every request eventually succeeds.
options.explanation: Unbounded retries multiply load on an already struggling dependency and exhaust worker pools.

options.label: Enforce strict latency budgets, bounded jittered retries, and graceful fallback or load shedding.
options.explanation: Bounding retries and isolating slow paths preserves healthy capacity and keeps tail latency predictable.

learningJourney.title: Social Graph Service & Hybrid Fan-Out Workers
learningJourney.purpose: Route normal vs. celebrity posts dynamically using sharded follower adjacency lists.

explanation.foundation: Fan-Out Workers query the Social Graph Service (sharded Redis/TAO-style graph cache backed by MySQL/Cassandra) for the author's `follower_count` and active follower IDs.
explanation.core: Authors `< 100K` followers fan out to follower Redis `ZSET`s (`ZADD` + `ZREMRANGEBYRANK` cap 800).

sectionDiagram.title: Social Graph + Push/Pull Split

cards.label: Dead-Letter Isolation
cards.detail: Route mega-fanout retries to a separate Kafka DLQ so one glitch doesn't stall normal posts.

cards.label: Graph Caching
cards.detail: Cache follower lists in Redis/TAO with write-through invalidation on follow/unfollow.

sectionDiagram.summary: Social Graph caching and threshold splitting keep fan-out workers fast under celebrity bursts.
sectionDiagram.caption: Isolated retry queues prevent single-author glitches from blocking global timelines.

learningJourney.title: Two-Stage Feed Hydrator & Feature Store
learningJourney.purpose: Merge push inboxes, celebrity pulls, and out-of-network candidates under 40ms.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Two-Stage Feed Hydrator & Feature Store** as the intuition layer for Design a Global Social Media Newsfeed & Timeline Engine (300M DAU): Merge push inboxes, celebrity pulls, and out-of-network candidates under 40ms.
explanation.core: On `GET /v1/feed`, the Timeline Service fetches the user's inbox `ZSET` (top 400), pulls top 50 posts from followed celebrities, and queries an ANN vector index for 200 out-of-network 'For You' posts. The Hydrator runs parallel Redis `MGET`s for post/author objects, filters `blocked_authors`, and fetches user-author affinity features from a Redis Feature Store.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, two-stage feed hydrator & feature store becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Engineer 7-day rotating Seen-Post Bloom filters, 10m snapshot cursors, diversity decay, and non-jumping live pills.

sectionDiagram.title: Three-Source Candidate Merge & Hydration

cards.label: Timeout Budgets
cards.detail: Set a hard 25ms timeout on out-of-network ANN; serve in-network feed if ANN lags.

cards.label: Parallel Scatter
cards.detail: Execute inbox, celebrity, and OON fetches concurrently in one fan-out.

sectionDiagram.summary: Parallel candidate fetching and batched MGET hydration assemble 650+ candidates in <40ms.
sectionDiagram.caption: Hard timeouts on discovery ANN keep core in-network timelines resilient.

learningJourney.title: LightGBM / Two-Tower ML Ranker & Diversity Pass
learningJourney.purpose: Maximize user engagement while enforcing author diversity and fallback safety.

explanation.foundation: Think of **LightGBM / Two-Tower ML Ranker & Diversity Pass** as the intuition layer for Design a Global Social Media Newsfeed & Timeline Engine (300M DAU): Maximize user engagement while enforcing author diversity and fallback safety.
explanation.core: The ML Ranking Service (GPU/CPU Triton inference) scores the ~650 hydrated candidates using LightGBM or a multi-task Deep Neural Network predicting `P(click)`, `P(like)`, `P(repost)`, and `P(negative_feedback)`. A Diversity Re-Ranker applies exponential author-repeat decay (`0.5^k`) and injects sponsored slots before returning the ranked list.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, lightgbm / two-tower ml ranker & diversity pass becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Engineer 7-day rotating Seen-Post Bloom filters, 10m snapshot cursors, diversity decay, and non-jumping live pills.

cards.label: Batch Inference
cards.detail: Score all 650 candidates in one vectorized Triton batch rather than per-item RPCs.

cards.label: Explainable Weights
cards.detail: Keep engagement-vs-recency weights configurable via dynamic experiment flags.

sectionDiagram.summary: Vectorized Triton scoring and author-decay re-ranking deliver personalized feeds in <40ms.
sectionDiagram.caption: Automatic chronological fallback guarantees zero downtime during ML deploys.

learningJourney.title: Seen-Post Bloom Filter & Snapshot Cursor Pagination
learningJourney.purpose: Eliminate already-viewed posts and guarantee smooth, duplicate-free infinite scroll.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Seen-Post Bloom Filter & Snapshot Cursor Pagination** as the intuition layer for Design a Global Social Media Newsfeed & Timeline Engine (300M DAU): Eliminate already-viewed posts and guarantee smooth, duplicate-free infinite scroll.
explanation.core: To avoid showing posts the user scrolled past 10 minutes ago, the Feed Service checks a per-user 7-day Seen-Post Bloom Filter (~2KB per active user in Redis, updated asynchronously by client viewport beacons). The final ranked list is stored as a 10-minute Feed Snapshot in Redis, returning an opaque Base64 cursor for instant <5ms page 2..N slices.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, seen-post bloom filter & snapshot cursor pagination becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Engineer 7-day rotating Seen-Post Bloom filters, 10m snapshot cursors, diversity decay, and non-jumping live pills.

cards.label: Rotating Daily Blooms

cards.label: Zero ML on Scroll

sectionDiagram.summary: Per-user rotating Bloom filters and 10m feed snapshots make infinite scroll fast and duplicate-free.
sectionDiagram.caption: Splitting 7-day seen history into daily bitsets enables effortless TTL expiration.

learningJourney.title: Multi-Region Active-Active & Live Streaming Updates
learningJourney.purpose: Scale globally across continents and push real-time 'New Posts' pills to active clients.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Multi-Region Active-Active & Live Streaming Updates** as the intuition layer for Design a Global Social Media Newsfeed & Timeline Engine (300M DAU): Scale globally across continents and push real-time 'New Posts' pills to active clients.
explanation.core: Each region hosts full Read/Cache/ML stacks with local Redis clusters and async cross-region Cassandra/Kafka replication for posts and social graph edges. For users actively viewing the top of their feed, lightweight SSE/WebSocket gateways subscribe to followed-author Redis Pub/Sub channels to display a non-disruptive '3 new posts' pill without jumping the scroll position.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, multi-region active-active & live streaming updates becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Engineer 7-day rotating Seen-Post Bloom filters, 10m snapshot cursors, diversity decay, and non-jumping live pills.

cards.label: Regional Isolation

sectionDiagram.summary: Regionalized read/ML stacks and non-disruptive live pills complete a global 300M-DAU timeline.
sectionDiagram.caption: Async cross-region post replication keeps multi-continent latency consistently low.

knowledgeChecks.question: How does caching a 150M-active-user Redis inbox tier (rather than all 300M+ registered accounts) affect system cost and correctness?

options.text: It cuts Redis RAM in half (~2TB saved) while dormant users who return simply fall back to a read-time DB merge.
options.feedback: Correct! Pushing only to recently active users saves massive RAM with a clean read-time fallback for dormant accounts.

options.text: Dormant users permanently lose all their posts.
options.feedback: All posts remain durably stored in Cassandra/MySQL; only the precomputed Redis cache is skipped.
Celebrity Fan-Out-on-Read is already computed at read time.
Media CDN is completely independent of Redis inbox caching.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Precomputing Redis timelines only for users active in the last 14-30 days slashes memory costs by 50-70% without losing data.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should a per-user 7-day Seen-Post Bloom Filter be implemented as 7 rotating daily filters instead of one single Bloom filter?

options.text: Standard Bloom filters do not support deletions; rotating 7 daily filters lets expired days drop via simple Redis TTLs.
options.feedback: Correct! Time-bucketed daily Bloom filters expire old items cleanly via Redis TTL without false-positive saturation.

options.text: Redis keys cannot be larger than 300 bytes.
options.feedback: Redis strings can be up to 512MB; rotation is for clean TTL expiration.

options.text: To force the ML ranker to run on every scroll page.
options.feedback: Scroll pages slice the cached snapshot without re-running ML.

options.text: Because Kafka only retains 1 day of data.
options.feedback: Kafka retention is unrelated to per-user Redis Bloom expiration.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: A single non-expiring Bloom filter eventually fills up and hits 100% false positives. Rotating 7 daily filters with 7-day TTLs keeps memory and FP rate constant.

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the best fallback if the Triton ML Ranking Service exceeds its 50ms latency budget during a traffic spike?

options.text: Return HTTP 500 Internal Server Error to the mobile app.
options.feedback: Failing the entire feed when chronological candidates are already hydrated ruins availability.

options.text: Degrade gracefully to reverse-chronological ordering of the hydrated in-network candidates.
options.feedback: Correct! Chronological fallback keeps feeds fast and available even if ML inference degrades.

options.text: Block the request for 10 seconds waiting for Triton.
options.feedback: Waiting 10s violates the <150ms p99 feed SLA.
The Social Graph is needed for fan-out, not ML fallback.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Because candidate IDs are already fetched and hydrated in chronological order, falling back to reverse-chronological sort on ML timeout preserves 99.99% feed availability.

beginner.summary: Design a 300M-user social media newsfeed that loads in under 150ms and handles viral celebrity posts.
beginner.keyTakeaway: To keep the architecture evolvable without sacrificing reliability, separate ingestion (Kafka partitioned by AuthorID + Media CDN) from Hybrid Fan-Out (active-only Redis ZSETs + Celebrity Pull Cache), Two-Stage ML Ranking, and Snapshot Cursor Pagination.
beginner.byteSummary:
At 300 million users, a newsfeed separates uploading photos (straight to a CDN) from building timelines. Normal users push new post IDs to active friends' Redis feeds, while celebrities wait for readers to pull their latest posts.

When you open the app, a fast ranker sorts the best posts, hides ones you already saw, and saves your scroll page so nothing repeats.

intermediate.summary: Architect 200K RPS reads, 2TB active-only Redis ZSETs, author-partitioned Kafka, and <40ms Triton ML ranking.
intermediate.keyTakeaway: To keep the architecture evolvable without sacrificing reliability, separate ingestion (Kafka partitioned by AuthorID + Media CDN) from Hybrid Fan-Out (active-only Redis ZSETs + Celebrity Pull Cache), Two-Stage ML Ranking, and Snapshot Cursor Pagination.
intermediate.byteSummary:
At 200K peak read RPS, media uploads go straight to S3/CDN while Kafka partitioned by `author_id` drives Hybrid Fan-Out across a 100K-follower threshold. Only 150M recently active users hold 800-item Redis `ZSET` inboxes (~2TB RAM).

Feed reads merge push inboxes, celebrity pulls, and out-of-network ANN candidates, hydrating via Redis `MGET` before <40ms LightGBM/DNN scoring with chronological timeout fallback.

advanced.summary: Engineer 7-day rotating Seen-Post Bloom filters, 10m snapshot cursors, diversity decay, and non-jumping live pills.
advanced.keyTakeaway: To keep the architecture evolvable without sacrificing reliability, separate ingestion (Kafka partitioned by AuthorID + Media CDN) from Hybrid Fan-Out (active-only Redis ZSETs + Celebrity Pull Cache), Two-Stage ML Ranking, and Snapshot Cursor Pagination.
advanced.byteSummary:
Duplicate-free infinite scroll relies on a 10-minute ranked Redis snapshot keyed by an opaque cursor (skipping ML on pages 2..N) and 7 rotating daily Seen-Post Bloom filters (~2KB/user) for clean TTL expiration.

Diversity re-ranking applies `0.5^k` author decay, hydration-time `blocked_authors` checks enforce instant safety, and regionalized stacks push non-jumping SSE 'New Posts' pills.
